7th - Schrodingers Leif 12/15/2025 7:41 PM
AHEM: INGREDIENTS
  • 1 can pureed tomato (around 2 cups worth. Should be
  • 1/2 cup Chardonay (honestly any white wine probably works, just used chardonay cause that was what my parents had/allowed me to use)
  • 1 1/2 shallot, finely chopped
  • salt (to taste)
  • olive oil (a teensy weensy bit, like a splash)
  • 3 sticks of rosemary
  • 4 sticks of oregano
  • heavy cream (~1 tbsp)
  • Gnocci (I just got it from the store and followed the directions)
STEPS 1. Chop shallots until they are fine. Put them in a pan with a splash of olive oil at medium heat. Let cook for 3-5 minutes or until semi-transluscent and starting to brown 2. Pour in chardonay, and add rosemary on top. Stir around until chardonay is reduced (essentially until the alchohol smell has dicipated, and around 1/2 of the chardonay is still there) 3. dump in the tomato puree. Add oregano, then add a splash of heavy cream. Add salt to taste. Set to low heat 4. wait like... 10-20 minutes, or until sauce starts to simmer. Remeber to stir semi-reguarly. 5. Cook Gnocci per instructions of bag. 6. Once sauce and gnocci are done, plate OPTIONAL: Add garlic. I was going to add garlic, specifically raosted, but I timed the roasting a bit off, so it came out after my sauce was done. (edited)

3rd - Gersh 12/19/2025 10:27 AM
Ok so my thoughts on this FTC, obviously I skew CJ because we worked together the entire game. But I think both have cases to make for why they should win.

CJ

CJ played a crucial role in the strategy of the game, he made himself an available number and for the most part was pretty calculated with his voting. Along with giving me space to make moves along the way, he was invited to the power alliance that ran the early to mid merge. And despite being on the bottom of the power alliance he won the challenges when he needed in order to keep his head above water. I think he can claim f8 and f6 pretty easily. I think he purposefully leaked the Leif plan at 8 so she would idol and Jah would go (he told me specifically that round he wanted Jah to go) and at 6 he planted the seed to me of making a move that round. I wanted to vote smite there but once things started getting scrambley I went to him about moving our votes to Saul and he was the one who got smite on board as well. With CJ I just need him to own the chaotic, messy nature of his game and explain how the chaos benefited him (because it really did benefit him a lot at times).

Smite

Small might played the floater strategy to a tee, and let the rest of the cast play each other out of the game while he kept threat levels to a minimum. Dude is a lawyer and I think maybe some people have forgotten that. He probably saw his life flash before his eyes at the double elim, and f8 and f7 he knew the exact pitch he needed to make and to who. Which landed him in the good graces of the power alliance. He was at a f6 with an alliance of 5 and himself and despite that, the tides changed exactly when he needed them to and he rode it to the end. If you think about it he held a lot of the power at f8 and f6 too. With smite I need him to talk out his strategy to me, because coordinating with him was… well. Most of the times the responses I got to long questions were “yep” so I need to know if he was actually coordinating with anyone. But he’s got the underdog story and if he hammers that I might be inclined to listen.
